issues.description: The problem text contains conflicting specifications for the milk method signature and expected output. In the UML and other parts of the statement the Milkable interface method is declared as messageOnMilk():String (no parameters), and the provided solution and template call/implement messageOnMilk() with no argument. However, Part 2 of the narrative (instructions for Part 2) states the method should be messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and specifies a return format including the milk volume. This mismatch between an interface with no parameter (UML, template usage, and solution) and the textual requirement (double parameter and volume in output) will confuse students about the correct method signature and expected output and may cause compilation or test failures depending on which spec they follow.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the contradiction by choosing one of the two consistent options: (A) If the intended design is a no-argument milk method, update the Part 2 textual description to specify messageOnMilk() with no parameters and clarify the expected return string (e.g., "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). Or (B) if the intended design is to include a milk volume, change the interface and all implementations/calls (Milkable.java, Seal/Goat classes, template Main, and tests) to messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and update implementations to return the specified string including "(volume: [milkVolume]L)". Align tests and examples accordingly so students have a single, consistent specification.
